title: A local tarball shadows a published version silently
foundBy: session agent, reviewing how local builds reach installs (tasks/pin-on-local-builds.md, section 9)

evidence.verified: TestALocalVersionWithOtherBytesThanThePublishedOneIsWarnedOf and TestADataDirectoryVersionWithOtherBytesThanItsImageIsWarnedOf pass under `go test ./internal/registry/ -count=1`. Through a project's scripts/with-npmrevs.sh, a data directory holding a left-pad 1.3.0 unlike npmjs.com's printed, as the wrapper stopped the registry, `a local version takes the place of a published one with other bytes`, naming both integrities. GitHub CI's `ci` passed on ebb13b8.

resolution: The local version is still served, as R9 and R24 require. The server now logs a warning once for each shadowing, naming the package, the version, the local file and both integrities (SPEC R9a). The projects' scripts/with-npmrevs.sh prints the registry's warnings when it stops it, so an install through it shows them.
details: A version in a data directory takes the place of the same version from an image or from the upstream (R9, R24), which is the point. When its bytes differ from the one it replaces, nothing says so. The install then records an integrity no published copy has, and the next machine that installs from the published one fails with EINTEGRITY. It should warn, naming both integrities.
